newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Honduras hunts for inmates after mass break-out.
newsitem.headline: Honduras hunts for inmates after mass break-out.

text.p: Police and troops on Tuesday searched for hundreds of prisoners, some of them dangerous felons, who escaped from jail in northwestern Honduras following a deadly prison riot.

Some 380 prisoners were still on the loose after about 480 of them broke free from a prison late on Monday near the town of Santa Barbara, 110 miles (180 km) northwest of the capital Tegucigalpa, police said.

"We have recaptured about 100 of the escaped prisoners and we have dispatched police to track down the remainder. We have received reinforcements for this task," Santa Barbara police chief Israel Mejia told Reuters.
The army set up roadblocks and police searched homes in nearby villages for the escaped criminals, who threw rocks at guards and set fire to the jail before busting out.
One prisoner was killed during the melee, although police had no details about how he died.

The inmates were angry at squalid prison conditions and a slow judicial system in this Central American nation that has left about 90 percent of prisoners languishing in jail without a formal sentence, according to official statistics.

"People are protesting because they suspended our daily visits and we live in bad conditions, there is hardly any room to stand in here," one inmate who identified himself as Cristobal Sagastume told Honduran radio late on Monday.
Honduras' Radio America said on Tuesday another group of about 50 escaped inmates had turned themselves in to authorities, but police were unable to confirm the report.

Television images on Tuesday showed the charred remains of the prison, which burned down almost entirely because there was no fire department in Santa Barbara, a town of some 35,000 residents. Witnesses said villagers used water hoses and buckets to help douse the flames until firemen arrived from the city of San Pedro Sula, a three-hour drive away.
Inmates also rioted and set a fire to another jail on Monday in the town of Trujillo, 180 miles (290 km) north of the capital, but officials said no prisoners had escaped or were injured.
Authorities on Tuesday said they had regained control of the Trujillo jail, but admitted that the riots were likely to raise questions abut the overtaxed judicial system.
"Our penitentiary system is an anachronism. The buildings to house prisoners were built last century and cannot cope," Romelia Garcia, the head of the prison system, told reporters.
